quotes.text: This she spoke with so commanding an air, standing with her back to the fire, with one hand behind her, and a pinch of snuff in the other, that I question whether Thalestris, at the head of her Amazons, ever made a more tremendous figure.
quotes.reference: 1749, Henry Fielding, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling:

translations.word: 令人敬畏/驚歎/驚異的 /令人敬畏/惊叹/惊异的

senses.definition: Notable for its size, power, or excellence.
examples: Van Beethoven's ninth symphony is a tremendous piece of music.

senses.definition: Extremely large (in amount, extent, degree, etc.) or great
examples: There was a tremendous outpouring of support.

quotes.text: The tremendous tragedy in which he had been involved - it was evident he was a fugitive from Weybridge - had driven him to the very verge of his reason.
quotes.reference: 1898, H.G. Wells, The War of the Worlds, London: William Heinemann, page 113:
